components.gap: Spencer s.4.1 (author copy s.1, pp.1-3): the simple unary predicate model SU(n,p), the YES sentence and its probability 1-(1-p)^n, the p(n)=c/n parametrization and threshold notion, and the remaining definitions, theorems with complete proofs, examples and limitations of that section are not present anywhere on the handbook route.

Only fixed-density G(n,p) (p constant, mainly p=1/2) appears. Spencer s.4.2 (author copy s.2, pp.3-5): G(n,p(n)) with p a function of n, threshold functions and the worked threshold examples (K4, triangle, no isolated vertex at n^{-1} ln n, connectivity), the evolution viewpoint and the p=n^{-alpha} regime are absent, with their exact hypotheses, complete proofs and failure boundaries.

Only one-vertex extension axioms for constant p are present. Spencer s.4.3 (author copy s.3, pp.5-7): rooted graphs (R,H), Ext(R,H), parameters r,v,e, dense/sparse via the sign of v-e*alpha with irrational alpha, rigid, safe, subextension and nailextension, the alpha=pi/7 examples, the statement that Ext(R,H) holds almost surely iff (R,H) is safe with its complete proof, and the rigid-extension discussion are absent.

Spencer s.4.4 (author copy s.4): t-closure cl_t, closure types via rigid extensions, the Finite Closure Lemma for G(n,n^{-alpha}) with alpha irrational and its proof, and the rest of the section are absent.
Spencer s.4.5 (author copy s.5): the almost sure theory T_alpha for p=n^{-alpha}, alpha irrational, its axioms, the zero-one law for that regime and its complete proof are absent.

The constant-p extension calculation n^{r+s}(1-p^r(1-p)^s)^{n-r-s} -> 0 and completeness by back-and-forth appear via Fagin 1976 (p09) and the p=1/2 paragraph (p03), but not Spencer s.4.6 as a presentation of SRC-050: the Alice Restaurant theory schema, the witness/independence argument as Spencer gives it, and the Duplicator strategy in the Ehrenfeucht game yielding the zero-one law for every constant 0<p<1, with SRC-050 citation and locators, are absent; a different source substitutes.

Uniqueness of the countable Rado graph for constant p is present (cited; back-and-forth only described). Spencer s.4.7 (author copy s.7, pp.13-14): the Godel-completeness argument that the almost sure theory has a countably infinite model, the explicit Left/Right-stage aleph_0-categoricity proof, and the proof that T_alpha for irrational alpha is not aleph_0-categorical (two constructions of distinct countable models) are absent.
Spencer s.4.8 (author copy s.8): the dynamic view of G(n,p) as p evolves and its results are absent.
Spencer s.4.9 (author copy s.9): infinite spectra via almost sure encoding, with its definitions, theorems and complete proofs, are absent.
Spencer s.4.10 (author copy s.10): the jump condition and its results with proofs are absent.
Spencer s.4.11 (author copy s.11): the complexity condition and its results with proofs are absent.
Spencer s.4.12 (author copy s.12): nonconvergence via almost sure encoding (sentences without a limiting probability) and its proofs are absent.
Spencer s.4.13 (author copy s.13): the result that evenness has no almost sure first-order representation, with proof, is absent.

The general Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse theorem appears only as a cited statement (thm:p03-ef, no proof). Spencer s.4.14 (author copy s.14, pp.26ff.): the graph game EHR(G,H;t) with board, players, play and winner, the theorem that Duplicator wins iff G,H agree on all sentences of quantifier depth t with complete proof, the isolated-vertex example and the remaining applications of the section are absent.
Spencer s.4.15 (author copy s.15): the survey of references with its attributions and stated limitations is absent.
